name: Remote patient monitoring and medical wearables
summary: Connected medical devices transmit health measurements from daily life into a clinical care pathway.
useCase: A care team reviews glucose or blood-pressure readings between appointments and contacts a patient when an agreed threshold is crossed.
whyNow: Connected glucose monitoring provides an established commercial base. The next phase is making remote measurements actionable, reimbursable and easy for patients to sustain across more conditions.

mainstream.scope: Covered chronic-disease pathways using validated devices and staffed clinical response, beyond already-established diabetes CGM.
mainstream.rationale: Device revenue growth and recognised remote monitoring workflows support near-term expansion. A wearable alone does not create clinical benefit: reliable data transmission and a care team’s response are necessary.

metric.name: Dexcom annual revenue
metric.scope: One continuous glucose monitoring supplier; adjacent clinical wearable proxy
metric.limitations: Company revenue is not the total RPM market, number of monitored patients or reimbursement spending. It measures CGM commercial scale, with product, pricing and geography effects. Latest full year is 2025.
metric.futureNote: No defensible like-for-like external forecast is available for this KPI. The forward maturity path is a separately labelled analyst scenario, not a numerical adoption forecast.

milestones.text: Revenue reached $4.662 billion; CMS issued guidance on correct use and billing of remote monitoring.
The February 2026 release reports the completed 2025 year. Current CMS guidance distinguishes connected monitoring from unsupported data collection.

tailwinds: Chronic conditions need information between clinic visits
Smaller connected devices reduce patient effort
Care teams can prioritise the patients whose readings change
bottlenecks: False alarms and incoming data can increase staff workload
Adherence and connectivity determine usable data
Payment and clinical responsibility vary across care settings
watchMetrics: Active monitored patients with adequate data continuity
Avoidable admissions and clinical outcomes versus a comparator
Clinician workload, intervention rates and payer renewal
